agent.system_template:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

_onefetch() {
    local i cur prev opts cmd
    COMPREPLY=()
    if [[ "${BASH_VERSINFO[0]}" -ge 4 ]]; then
        cur="$2"
    else
        cur="${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD]}"
    fi
    prev="$3"
    cmd=""
    opts=""

    for i in "${COMP_WORDS[@]:0:COMP_CWORD}"
    do
        case "${cmd},${i}" in
            ",$1")
                cmd="onefetch"
                ;;
            *)
                ;;
        esac
    done

    case "${cmd}" in
        onefetch)
            opts="-d -e -E -T -t -z -c -a -i -o -l -p -h -V --disabled-fields --no-title --number-of-authors --number-of-languages --number-of-file-churns --churn-pool-size --exclude --no-bots --no-merges --email --http-url --hide-token --include-hidden --type --text-colors --iso-time --number-separator --no-bold --ascii-input --ascii-colors --ascii-language --true-color --image --image-protocol --color-resolution --no-color-palette --no-art --nerd-fonts --output --generate --languages --package-managers --help --version [INPUT]"
            if [[ ${cur} == -* || ${COMP_CWORD} -eq 1 ]] ; then
                COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${opts}" -- "${cur}") )
                return 0
            fi
            case "${prev}" in
                --disabled-fields)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -W "project description head pending version created languages dependencies authors last-change contributors url commits churn lines-of-code size license" -- "${cur}"))

    sys.stderr.write("Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [INPUT]\n\n")
    sys.stderr.write("For more information, try '--help'.\n")
    sys.exit(2)


def die_usage_tip(msg, tip):
    sys.stderr.write(f"error: {msg}\n\n")
    sys.stderr.write(f"  tip: {tip}\n\n")
    sys.stderr.write("Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [INPUT]\n\n")
    sys.stderr.write("For more information, try '--help'.\n")
    sys.exit(2)


def die_value(optname, value, possible=None, tip=None, extra=None):
    sys.stderr.write(f"error: invalid value '{value}' for '{optname}'")
    if extra:
        sys.stderr.write(f": {extra}")
    sys.stderr.write("\n")
    if possible is not None:
        sys.stderr.write(f"  [possible values: {', '.join(possible)}]\n")
    sys.stderr.write("\n")
    if tip:
        sys.stderr.write(f"  tip: {tip}\n\n")
    sys.stderr.write("For more information, try '--help'.\n")
    sys.exit(2)


def die_missing(optname, possible=None):
    sys.stderr.write(f"error: a value is required for '{optname}' but none was supplied\n")
    if possible is not None:
        sys.stderr.write(f"  [possible values: {', '.join(possible)}]\n")
    sys.stderr.write("\n")
    sys.stderr.write("For more information, try '--help'.\n")
    sys.exit(2)


def similar_name(value, candidates):
    """Simple similarity: pick candidate with smallest edit distance."""
    if not candidates:
        return None
    best = None
    best_d = None
    for c in candidates:
        d = edit_distance(value, c)
        if best_d is None or d < best_d:
            best_d = d
            best = c
    if best_d is not None and best_d <= max(2, len(value) // 2):
        return best
    return None


def edit_distance(a, b):
    la, lb = len(a), len(b)
    dp = list(range(lb + 1))
    for i in range(1, la + 1):
        prev = dp[0]
        dp[0] = i
        for j in range(1, lb + 1):
            tmp = dp[j]
            if a[i-1] == b[j-1]:
                dp[j] = prev
            else:
                dp[j] = 1 + min(prev, dp[j], dp[j-1])
            prev = tmp
    return dp[lb]

def find_opt(token):
    """Return option spec matching token (for --long or -short)."""
    # token may be --name=value or --name
    name = token.split("=", 1)[0] if token.startswith("--") else token
    for spec in OPTIONS:
        lg, sh, kind, valn, poss, attr = spec
        if name == lg:
            return spec
        if sh is not None and name == sh:
            return spec
    return None


def parse_args(argv):
    args = Args()
    i = 0
    # Multi-value options need to accept multiple consecutive non-option tokens.
    positional = []
    while i < len(argv):
        tok = argv[i]
        if tok == "--":
            i += 1
            # All remaining are positional
            while i < len(argv):
                positional.append(argv[i])
                i += 1
            break
        # Handle help/version first
        if tok in ("-h", "--help"):
            if tok == "-h":
                sys.stdout.write(RESOURCES["help_short.txt"])
            else:
                sys.stdout.write(RESOURCES["help_long.txt"])
            sys.exit(0)
        if tok in ("-V", "--version"):
            sys.stdout.write(VERSION + "\n")
            sys.exit(0)
        if tok.startswith("-") and tok != "-":
            spec = find_opt(tok)
            if spec is None:
                # might be bundled short? onefetch doesn't seem to allow that so error.
                die_usage_tip(f"unexpected argument '{tok}' found",
                              f"to pass '{tok}' as a value, use '-- {tok}'")
            lg, sh, kind, valn, poss, attr = spec
            optname = f"{lg}"
            if valn:
                optname_disp = f"{lg} {valn}" if sh or True else lg
            # Build the display form used in errors
            if kind == "multi" or kind == "multi6":
                optname_disp = f"{lg} {valn}"
            elif kind == "num":
                optname_disp = f"{lg} {valn}"
            elif kind == "single":
                optname_disp = f"{lg} {valn}"
            elif kind == "optval":
                optname_disp = f"{lg}[={valn}]"
            else:
                optname_disp = lg
            # Get value (supports --opt=val and --opt val)
            has_eq = tok.startswith("--") and "=" in tok
            eq_value = None
            if has_eq:
                eq_value = tok.split("=", 1)[1]
            if kind == "flag":
                if has_eq:
                    die_usage(f"unexpected value '{eq_value}' for '{lg}' found; no more were expected")
                setattr(args, attr, True)
                i += 1
                continue
            if kind == "optval":
                # --no-bots can be alone or --no-bots=REGEX
                if getattr(args, attr + "_set", False):
                    # already set, error
                    die_usage(f"the argument '{optname_disp}' cannot be used multiple times")
                if has_eq:
                    setattr(args, attr, eq_value)
                else:
                    setattr(args, attr, "")
                setattr(args, attr + "_set", True)
                i += 1
                continue
            if kind == "num":
                if has_eq:
                    val = eq_value
                    i += 1
                else:
                    if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                        die_missing(optname_disp)
                    val = argv[i + 1]
                    i += 2
                try:
                    n = int(val)
                    if n < 0:
                        raise ValueError()
                    # Also rust's parse::<usize> rejects strings with leading '-'
                    if val.startswith("-"):
                        raise ValueError()
                except ValueError:
                    die_value(optname_disp, val, extra="invalid digit found in string")
                setattr(args, attr, n)
                continue
            if kind == "single":
                if has_eq:
                    val = eq_value
                    i += 1
                else:
                    if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                        die_missing(optname_disp, possible=poss)
                    val = argv[i + 1]
                    i += 2
                if poss is not None and val not in poss:
                    tip = None
                    # clap suggests a similar value
                    sim = similar_name(val, poss)
                    if sim:
                        tip = f"a similar value exists: '{sim}'"
                    die_value(optname_disp, val, possible=poss, tip=tip)
                setattr(args, attr, val)
                continue
            if kind in ("multi", "multi6"):
                # consume value(s)
                max_vals = 6 if kind == "multi6" else None
                collected = []
                if has_eq:
                    collected.append(eq_value)
                    i += 1
                else:
                    # need at least 1 value
                    if i + 1 >= len(argv) or argv[i + 1].startswith("-"):
                        die_missing(optname_disp)
                    i += 1
                # consume more non-option tokens up to max
                while i < len(argv):
                    if max_vals is not None and len(collected) >= max_vals:
                        break
                    nxt = argv[i]
                    if nxt.startswith("-") and nxt != "-":
                        break
                    collected.append(nxt)
                    i += 1
                # validate
                cur = getattr(args, attr)
                for v in collected:
                    if kind == "multi6":
                        # text-colors: must be int in 0..16
                        try:
                            iv = int(v)
                            if v.startswith("-"):
                                raise ValueError()
                        except ValueError:
                            die_value(optname_disp, v, extra="invalid digit found in string")
                        if iv < 0 or iv >= 16:
                            die_value(optname_disp, v, extra="%s is not in 0..16" % v)
                    if poss is not None and v not in poss:
                        die_value(optname_disp, v, possible=poss)
                # If option used multiple times, behavior differs. Let's append.
                if cur and attr == "type":
                    # first time overrides default
                    # Actually, we'll just accumulate across invocations
                    cur.extend(collected)
                else:
                    if attr == "type":
                        setattr(args, attr, list(collected))
                    else:
                        if not getattr(args, attr):
                            setattr(args, attr, [])
                        getattr(args, attr).extend(collected)
                continue
        else:
            positional.append(tok)
            i += 1
    if len(positional) > 1:
        die_usage(f"unexpected argument '{positional[1]}' found")
    if positional:
        args.input = positional[0]
    return args


# --- Resource handling ---

def load_resources_inline():
    """Resources are embedded as a base64 block at the end of this file."""
    global RESOURCES
    # Parse marker
    try:
        idx = __RESOURCES_B64__
    except NameError:
        return
    import zlib
    raw = zlib.decompress(base64.b64decode(idx))
    # Format: for each entry: name\n<len>\n<data>
    pos = 0
    data = raw
    while pos < len(data):
        nl = data.index(b"\n", pos)
        name = data[pos:nl].decode()
        pos = nl + 1
        nl2 = data.index(b"\n", pos)
        length = int(data[pos:nl2])
        pos = nl2 + 1
        content = data[pos:pos+length].decode()
        pos += length
        RESOURCES[name] = content


# --- Git repo analysis ---

def run_git(cwd, *args):
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["git"] + list(args), cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False
        )
        return result.returncode, result.stdout, result.stderr
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return 127, "", "git not found"


def find_repo(path):
    """Walk up to find a .git dir or file. Return (repo_root, git_dir) or None."""
    p = os.path.abspath(path)
    while True:
        g = os.path.join(p, ".git")
        if os.path.exists(g):
            return p, g
        parent = os.path.dirname(p)
        if parent == p:
            return None
        p = parent


def git_version():
    rc, out, _ = run_git(None, "--version")
    if rc == 0:
        return out.strip()
    return ""


def short_sha(cwd, ref):
    rc, out, _ = run_git(cwd, "rev-parse", "--short", ref)
    if rc == 0:
        return out.strip()
    return ""


def head_refs(cwd):
    sha = short_sha(cwd, "HEAD")
    rc, out, _ = run_git(cwd, "branch", "--show-current")
    refs = []
    if rc == 0 and out.strip():
        refs.append(out.strip())
    # Add tags
    rc, out, _ = run_git(cwd, "tag", "--points-at", "HEAD")
    if rc == 0:
        for line in out.strip().splitlines():
            if line.strip():
                refs.append(line.strip())
    return sha, refs


def pending_info(cwd):
    rc, out, _ = run_git(cwd, "status", "--porcelain")
    added = deleted = modified = 0
    if rc == 0:
        for line in out.splitlines():
            if len(line) < 2:
                continue
            xy = line[:2]
            if "?" in xy or "A" in xy:
                added += 1
            elif "D" in xy:
                deleted += 1
            elif "M" in xy or "R" in xy or "C" in xy or "U" in xy or "T" in xy:
                modified += 1
    return added, deleted, modified


def created_and_last_change(cwd, iso=False):
    # first commit and last commit
    rc, first, _ = run_git(cwd, "log", "--reverse", "--pretty=format:%at", "--max-parents=0")
    rc2, last, _ = run_git(cwd, "log", "-1", "--pretty=format:%at")
    def fmt(ts):
        if iso:
            return datetime.fromtimestamp(int(ts), tz=timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
        return humanize_ago(int(ts))
    created = ""
    last_change = ""
    if rc == 0 and first.strip():
        first_ts = first.strip().splitlines()[0]
        created = fmt(first_ts)
    if rc2 == 0 and last.strip():
        last_change = fmt(last.strip())
    return created, last_change


def humanize_ago(ts):
    now = int(datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc).timestamp())
    diff = now - ts
    if diff < 60:
        return "now"
    minutes = diff // 60
    if minutes < 60:
        return f"{minutes} minute{'s' if minutes != 1 else ''} ago"
    hours = minutes // 60
    if hours < 24:
        return f"{hours} hour{'s' if hours != 1 else ''} ago"
    days = hours // 24
    if days < 7:
        return f"{days} day{'s' if days != 1 else ''} ago"
    weeks = days // 7
    if weeks < 5:
        return f"{weeks} week{'s' if weeks != 1 else ''} ago"
    months = days // 30
    if months < 12:
        return f"{months} month{'s' if months != 1 else ''} ago"
    years = days // 365
    return f"{years} year{'s' if years != 1 else ''} ago"


def list_files(cwd):
    rc, out, _ = run_git(cwd, "ls-files")
    if rc != 0:
        return []
    return [f for f in out.splitlines() if f.strip()]


def authors_info(cwd, limit, show_email=False):
    rc, out, _ = run_git(cwd, "log", "--pretty=format:%an|%ae")
    if rc != 0:
        return [], 0
    counts = {}
    emails = {}
    total = 0
    for line in out.splitlines():
        if "|" in line:
            name, email = line.split("|", 1)
        else:
            name, email = line, ""
        counts[name] = counts.get(name, 0) + 1
        emails.setdefault(name, email)
        total += 1
    sorted_a = sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda x: (-x[1], x[0]))
    result = []
    for name, n in sorted_a[:limit]:
        contribution = int(round(100.0 * n / total)) if total else 0
        result.append({
            "name": name,
            "email": emails[name] if show_email else None,
            "nbrOfCommits": n,
            "contribution": contribution,
        })
    return result, len(counts)


def total_commits(cwd):
    rc, out, _ = run_git(cwd, "rev-list", "--count", "HEAD")
    if rc == 0:
        return int(out.strip())
    return 0


def is_shallow(cwd):
    rc, out, _ = run_git(cwd, "rev-parse", "--is-shallow-repository")
    return out.strip() == "true"


def churn_info(cwd, limit, pool_size=None):
    # How many commits to consider?
    pool = pool_size if pool_size is not None else total_commits(cwd)
    rc, out, _ = run_git(cwd, "log", f"-n{pool}", "--name-only", "--pretty=format:")
    if rc != 0:
        return [], pool
    counts = {}
    for line in out.splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if line:
            counts[line] = counts.get(line, 0) + 1
    sorted_c = sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda x: (-x[1], x[0]))
    out_list = [{"filePath": f, "nbrOfCommits": c} for f, c in sorted_c[:limit]]
    return out_list, pool


def repo_size_and_file_count(cwd):
    rc, out, _ = run_git(cwd, "ls-tree", "-r", "-l", "HEAD")
    if rc != 0:
        return "0 B", 0
    total = 0
    count = 0
    for line in out.splitlines():
        parts = line.split()
        if len(parts) >= 4:
            try:
                total += int(parts[3])
                count += 1
            except ValueError:
                pass
    return human_size(total), count


def human_size(n):
    units = ["B", "KiB", "MiB", "GiB", "TiB"]
    i = 0
    f = float(n)
    while f >= 1024 and i < len(units) - 1:
        f /= 1024
        i += 1
    if i == 0:
        return f"{int(f)} {units[i]}"
    # 1 decimal to 2 sig figs
    if f >= 100:
        return f"{f:.0f} {units[i]}"
    return f"{f:.2f} {units[i]}"


def detect_license(cwd):
    for name in os.listdir(cwd):
        if name.upper().startswith("LICENSE") or name.upper().startswith("LICENCE") or name.upper().startswith("COPYING"):
            try:
                with open(os.path.join(cwd, name), "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
                    content = f.read()
                # Very simple detection
                if "MIT License" in content or "MIT LICENSE" in content.upper():
                    return "MIT"
                if "Apache License" in content:
                    return "Apache-2.0"
                if "GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE" in content.upper():
                    return "GPL"
                if "BSD" in content:
                    return "BSD"
                return ""
            except OSError:
                pass
    return ""


def repo_name(cwd):
    # Try remote URL
    rc, out, _ = run_git(cwd, "config", "--get", "remote.origin.url")
    if rc == 0 and out.strip():
        url = out.strip()
        name = url.rstrip("/").split("/")[-1]
        if name.endswith(".git"):
            name = name[:-4]
        return name, url
    return "", ""


def detect_languages(cwd, files, types_filter):
    """Very basic language detection based on file extensions."""
    # Count bytes per language
    ext_map = {
        ".py": ("Python", "programming"),
        ".rs": ("Rust", "programming"),
        ".c": ("C", "programming"),
        ".h": ("C Header", "programming"),
        ".cpp": ("C++", "programming"),
        ".cc": ("C++", "programming"),
        ".hpp": ("C++", "programming"),
        ".go": ("Go", "programming"),
        ".java": ("Java", "programming"),
        ".js": ("JavaScript", "programming"),
        ".ts": ("TypeScript", "programming"),
        ".jsx": ("JSX", "programming"),
        ".tsx": ("TSX", "programming"),
        ".sh": ("Shell", "programming"),
        ".rb": ("Ruby", "programming"),
        ".php": ("PHP", "programming"),
        ".md": ("Markdown", "prose"),
        ".html": ("HTML", "markup"),
        ".css": ("CSS", "markup"),
        ".xml": ("XML", "data"),
        ".json": ("JSON", "data"),
        ".yml": ("YAML", "data"),
        ".yaml": ("YAML", "data"),
        ".toml": ("TOML", "data"),
        ".txt": ("Plain Text", "prose"),
    }
    counts = {}
    total = 0
    for f in files:
        full = os.path.join(cwd, f)
        try:
            size = os.path.getsize(full)
        except OSError:
            continue
        _, ext = os.path.splitext(f)
        ext = ext.lower()
        if ext in ext_map:
            lang, ty = ext_map[ext]
            if ty in types_filter:
                counts[lang] = counts.get(lang, 0) + size
                total += size
    if total == 0:
        return []
    items = sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])
    return [{"language": k, "percentage": round(v * 100.0 / total, 1)} for k, v in items]


def lines_of_code(cwd, files, types_filter):
    """Count total lines of code across known source files."""
    total = 0
    ext_map = {".py",".rs",".c",".h",".cpp",".cc",".hpp",".go",".java",".js",".ts",".jsx",".tsx",".sh",".rb",".php"}
    for f in files:
        _, ext = os.path.splitext(f)
        if ext.lower() not in ext_map:
            continue
        full = os.path.join(cwd, f)
        try:
            with open(full, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fp:
                for line in fp:
                    total += 1
        except OSError:
            pass
    return total


# --- Output builders ---

def format_number(n, sep):
    s = str(n)
    if sep == "plain":
        return s
    m = {"comma": ",", "space": " ", "underscore": "_"}.get(sep, "")
    # Group by 3 from right
    parts = []
    i = len(s)
    while i > 3:
        parts.insert(0, s[i-3:i])
        i -= 3
    parts.insert(0, s[:i])
    return m.join(parts)


def build_info_struct(args, cwd):
    repoName, repoUrl = repo_name(cwd)
    sha, refs = head_refs(cwd)
    added, deleted, modified = pending_info(cwd)
    created, last_change = created_and_last_change(cwd, iso=args.iso_time)
    authors_list, total_authors = authors_info(cwd, args.number_of_authors, show_email=args.email)
    commits_n = total_commits(cwd)
    shallow = is_shallow(cwd)
    files = list_files(cwd)
    types_filter = set(args.type)
    langs = detect_languages(cwd, files, types_filter)
    loc = lines_of_code(cwd, files, types_filter)
    churns, pool = churn_info(cwd, args.number_of_file_churns, pool_size=args.churn_pool_size)
    size, file_count = repo_size_and_file_count(cwd)
    license_name = detect_license(cwd)

    info_fields = []

    def disabled(name):
        return name in args.disabled_fields

    if not disabled("project"):
        info_fields.append({"ProjectInfo": {"repoName": repoName, "numberOfBranches": 0, "numberOfTags": 0}})
    if not disabled("description"):

def get_git_username(cwd):
    # onefetch uses project directory name in some contexts, here we use user.name
    rc, out, _ = run_git(cwd, "config", "--get", "user.name")
    if rc == 0 and out.strip():
        return out.strip()
    return ""


def to_yaml(data, indent=0):
    """Very simple YAML serializer matching observed format."""
    out = []
    prefix = "  " * indent
    if isinstance(data, dict):
        for k, v in data.items():
            if isinstance(v, (dict, list)):
                if isinstance(v, list) and not v:
                    out.append(f"{prefix}{k}: []")
                elif isinstance(v, dict) and not v:
                    out.append(f"{prefix}{k}: {{}}")
                else:
                    out.append(f"{prefix}{k}:")
                    out.append(to_yaml(v, indent + 1))
            else:
                out.append(f"{prefix}{k}: {yaml_scalar(v)}")
    elif isinstance(data, list):
        for item in data:
            if isinstance(item, dict):
                # First key goes with dash
                keys = list(item.keys())
                first_k = keys[0]
                first_v = item[first_k]
                if isinstance(first_v, (dict, list)):
                    out.append(f"{prefix}- {first_k}:")
                    out.append(to_yaml(first_v, indent + 2))
                else:
                    out.append(f"{prefix}- {first_k}: {yaml_scalar(first_v)}")
                for k in keys[1:]:
                    v = item[k]
                    if isinstance(v, (dict, list)):
                        out.append(f"{prefix}  {k}:")
                        out.append(to_yaml(v, indent + 2))
                    else:
                        out.append(f"{prefix}  {k}: {yaml_scalar(v)}")
            else:
                out.append(f"{prefix}- {yaml_scalar(item)}")
    return "\n".join(out)


def yaml_scalar(v):
    if v is None:
        return "null"
    if isinstance(v, bool):
        return "true" if v else "false"
    if isinstance(v, (int, float)):
        return str(v)
    if isinstance(v, str):
        if v == "":
            return "''"
        return v
    return str(v)

    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(data, indent=2))
    sys.stdout.flush()


def output_yaml(data):
    sys.stdout.write(to_yaml(data))
    sys.stdout.write("\n")

    if args.package_managers_flag:
        sys.stdout.write(RESOURCES["package_managers.txt"])

            "fish": "complete_fish.fish",
            "powershell": "complete_pwsh.ps1",
            "elvish": "complete_elvish.elv",

        sys.stdout.write(RESOURCES[keymap[args.generate]])
        return 0

    # Determine working directory
    path = args.input or os.getcwd()
    if not os.path.isdir(path):
        sys.stderr.write(f"Error: Failed to access a directory, or path is not a directory: '{path}'\n")
        return 1
    abspath = os.path.abspath(path)

    if args.image is not None:

            sys.stderr.write(f"Error: Could not load the image file at '{args.image}'\n\n")
            sys.stderr.write("Caused by:\n")

            return 1

def render_terminal(args, data, cwd):
    """Terminal render: print title header and info lines with ANSI colors."""
    # Very basic rendering; not attempting to match ASCII art
    # Based on observed output: header includes user, separator, fields with colon
    # Using [37;1m style bold ANSI for labels.
    BOLD = "\033[1m"
    RESET = "\033[0m"
    # Colors indices: title=37;1 ~=39;1 underline=37;1 subtitle=39;1 colon=39;1 info=39
    # Allow override via args.text_colors
    def esc(code):
        return f"\033[{code}m"
    tcols = args.text_colors if args.text_colors else []
    def c(idx, default):
        if idx < len(tcols):
            n = int(tcols[idx])
            # ANSI 30+ for base; clap converts 0..15 to escapes
            # 0-7 -> 30-37, 8-15 -> 90-97
            if n < 8:
                return f"{30 + n};1"
            else:
                return f"{90 + (n - 8)};1"
        return default
    title_c = c(0, "37;1")
    tilde_c = c(1, "39;1")
    underline_c = c(2, "37;1")
    subtitle_c = c(3, "39;1")
    colon_c = c(4, "39;1")
    info_c = c(5, "39")
    if args.no_bold:
        # Remove ";1" from codes
        def strip1(x):
            return x.replace(";1", "")
        title_c = strip1(title_c)
        tilde_c = strip1(tilde_c)
        underline_c = strip1(underline_c)
        subtitle_c = strip1(subtitle_c)
        colon_c = strip1(colon_c)
        info_c = strip1(info_c)

    sys.stdout.write("\033[?7l")
    title = data["title"]
    user = title["gitUsername"]
    gv = title["gitVersion"]
    header = f"{esc(title_c)}{user}\033[0m {esc(tilde_c)}~\033[0m {esc(title_c)}{gv}\033[0m"
    sys.stdout.write(header + "\n")
    # underline length = len(user + " ~ " + gv) without ANSI
    plain_len = len(user) + 3 + len(gv)
    sys.stdout.write(f"{esc(underline_c.replace(';1',''))}" + "-" * plain_len + "\033[39m\n")
    # each info field
    for field in data["infoFields"]:
        key, val = next(iter(field.items()))
        rendered = render_field(key, val, args)
        for line in rendered:
            sys.stdout.write(
                f"{esc(subtitle_c)}{line['label']}\033[0m{esc(colon_c)}{line.get('colon',':')}\033[0m {esc(info_c)}{line['value']}\033[0m\n"
                if line.get('label') else
                f"{esc(info_c)}{line['value']}\033[0m\n"
            )
    # Color palette
    sys.stdout.write("\n")
    palette = ""
    for i in range(8):
        palette += f"\033[4{i}m   \033[49m"
    sys.stdout.write(palette + "\n")
    sys.stdout.write("\033[?7h")


def render_field(key, val, args):
    out = []
    if key == "HeadInfo":
        hr = val["headRefs"]
        refs = ", ".join(hr["refs"]) if hr["refs"] else ""
        v = hr["shortCommitId"]
        if refs:
            v += f" ({refs})"
        out.append({"label": "HEAD", "value": v})
    elif key == "PendingInfo":
        parts = []
        if val["added"]:
            parts.append(f"{val['added']}+")
        if val["deleted"]:
            parts.append(f"{val['deleted']}-")
        if val["modified"]:
            parts.append(f"{val['modified']}M")
        out.append({"label": "Pending", "value": " ".join(parts)})
    elif key == "CreatedInfo":
        out.append({"label": "Created", "value": val["creationDate"]})
    elif key == "AuthorsInfo":
        authors = val["authors"]
        if authors:
            for i, a in enumerate(authors):
                label = "Author" if i == 0 else ""
                v = f"{a['contribution']}% {a['name']} {a['nbrOfCommits']}"
                if a.get("email"):
                    v = f"{a['contribution']}% {a['name']} <{a['email']}> {a['nbrOfCommits']}"
                out.append({"label": label, "value": v, "colon": ":" if i == 0 else " "})
    elif key == "LastChangeInfo":
        out.append({"label": "Last change", "value": val["lastChange"]})
    elif key == "CommitsInfo":
        v = str(val["numberOfCommits"])
        if val["isShallow"]:
            v += " (shallow)"
        out.append({"label": "Commits", "value": v})
    elif key == "ChurnInfo":
        churns = val["file_churns"]
        if churns:
            pool = val["churn_pool_size"]
            for i, fc in enumerate(churns):
                label = f"Churn ({pool})" if i == 0 else ""
                v = f"{fc['filePath']} {fc['nbrOfCommits']}"
                out.append({"label": label, "value": v})
    elif key == "LocInfo":
        out.append({"label": "Lines of code", "value": str(val["linesOfCode"])})
    elif key == "SizeInfo":
        out.append({"label": "Size", "value": f"{val['repoSize']} ({val['fileCount']} file{'s' if val['fileCount']!=1 else ''})"})
    elif key == "LicenseInfo":
        if val["license"]:
            out.append({"label": "License", "value": val["license"]})
    elif key == "LanguagesInfo":
        langs = val["languagesWithPercentage"]
        if langs:
            parts = ", ".join(f"{l['language']} ({l['percentage']} %)" for l in langs)
            out.append({"label": "Language", "value": parts})
    elif key == "UrlInfo":
        if val.get("repoUrl"):
            out.append({"label": "URL", "value": val["repoUrl"]})
    return out


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        rc = main(sys.argv[1:])

    except BrokenPipeError:

def similar_name(value, candidates):
    """Simple similarity: pick candidate with smallest edit distance."""
    if not candidates:
        return None
    best = None
    best_d = None
    for c in candidates:
        d = edit_distance(value, c)
        if best_d is None or d < best_d:
            best_d = d
            best = c
    if best_d is not None and best_d <= max(2, len(value) // 2):
        return best
    return None


def edit_distance(a, b):
    la, lb = len(a), len(b)
    dp = list(range(lb + 1))
    for i in range(1, la + 1):
        prev = dp[0]
        dp[0] = i
        for j in range(1, lb + 1):
            tmp = dp[j]
            if a[i-1] == b[j-1]:
                dp[j] = prev
            else:
                dp[j] = 1 + min(prev, dp[j], dp[j-1])
            prev = tmp
    return dp[lb]

                if has_eq:
                    collected.append(eq_value)
                    i += 1
                else:
                    # need at least 1 value
                    if i + 1 >= len(argv) or argv[i + 1].startswith("-"):
                        die_missing(optname_disp)
                    i += 1
                # consume more non-option tokens up to max
                while i < len(argv):
                    if max_vals is not None and len(collected) >= max_vals:
                        break
                    nxt = argv[i]
                    if nxt.startswith("-") and nxt != "-":
                        break
                    collected.append(nxt)
                    i += 1
                # validate
                cur = getattr(args, attr)
                for v in collected:
                    if kind == "multi6":
                        # text-colors: must be int in 0..16
                        try:
                            iv = int(v)
                            if v.startswith("-"):
                                raise ValueError()
                        except ValueError:
                            die_value(optname_disp, v, extra="invalid digit found in string")
                        if iv < 0 or iv >= 16:
                            die_value(optname_disp, v, extra="%s is not in 0..16" % v)
                    if poss is not None and v not in poss:
                        die_value(optname_disp, v, possible=poss)
                # If option used multiple times, behavior differs. Let's append.
                if cur and attr == "type":
                    # first time overrides default
                    # Actually, we'll just accumulate across invocations
                    cur.extend(collected)
                else:
                    if attr == "type":
                        setattr(args, attr, list(collected))
                    else:
                        if not getattr(args, attr):
                            setattr(args, attr, [])
                        getattr(args, attr).extend(collected)
                continue
        else:
            positional.append(tok)
            i += 1
    if len(positional) > 1:
        die_usage(f"unexpected argument '{positional[1]}' found")
    if positional:
        args.input = positional[0]
    return args


# --- Resource handling ---

def load_resources_inline():
    """Resources are embedded as a base64 block at the end of this file."""
    global RESOURCES
    # Parse marker
    try:
        idx = __RESOURCES_B64__
    except NameError:
        return
    import zlib
    raw = zlib.decompress(base64.b64decode(idx))
    # Format: for each entry: name\n<len>\n<data>
    pos = 0
    data = raw
    while pos < len(data):
        nl = data.index(b"\n", pos)
        name = data[pos:nl].decode()
        pos = nl + 1
        nl2 = data.index(b"\n", pos)
        length = int(data[pos:nl2])
        pos = nl2 + 1
        content = data[pos:pos+length].decode()
        pos += length
        RESOURCES[name] = content


# --- Git repo analysis ---

def run_git(cwd, *args):
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["git"] + list(args), cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False
        )
        return result.returncode, result.stdout, result.stderr
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return 127, "", "git not found"


def find_repo(path):
    """Walk up to find a .git dir or file. Return (repo_root, git_dir) or None."""
    p = os.path.abspath(path)
    while True:
        g = os.path.join(p, ".git")
        if os.path.exists(g):
            return p, g
        parent = os.path.dirname(p)
        if parent == p:
            return None
        p = parent


def git_version():
    rc, out, _ = run_git(None, "--version")
    if rc == 0:
        return out.strip()
    return ""


def short_sha(cwd, ref):
    rc, out, _ = run_git(cwd, "rev-parse", "--short", ref)
    if rc == 0:
        return out.strip()
    return ""


def head_refs(cwd):
    sha = short_sha(cwd, "HEAD")
    rc, out, _ = run_git(cwd, "branch", "--show-current")
    refs = []
    if rc == 0 and out.strip():
        refs.append(out.strip())
    # Add tags
    rc, out, _ = run_git(cwd, "tag", "--points-at", "HEAD")
    if rc == 0:
        for line in out.strip().splitlines():
            if line.strip():
                refs.append(line.strip())
    return sha, refs


def pending_info(cwd):
    rc, out, _ = run_git(cwd, "status", "--porcelain")
    added = deleted = modified = 0
    if rc == 0:
        for line in out.splitlines():
            if len(line) < 2:
                continue
            xy = line[:2]
            if "?" in xy or "A" in xy:
                added += 1
            elif "D" in xy:
                deleted += 1
            elif "M" in xy or "R" in xy or "C" in xy or "U" in xy or "T" in xy:
                modified += 1
    return added, deleted, modified


def created_and_last_change(cwd, iso=False):
    # first commit and last commit
    rc, first, _ = run_git(cwd, "log", "--reverse", "--pretty=format:%at", "--max-parents=0")
    rc2, last, _ = run_git(cwd, "log", "-1", "--pretty=format:%at")
    def fmt(ts):
        if iso:
            return datetime.fromtimestamp(int(ts), tz=timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
        return humanize_ago(int(ts))
    created = ""
    last_change = ""
    if rc == 0 and first.strip():
        first_ts = first.strip().splitlines()[0]
        created = fmt(first_ts)
    if rc2 == 0 and last.strip():
        last_change = fmt(last.strip())
    return created, last_change


def humanize_ago(ts):
    now = int(datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc).timestamp())
    diff = now - ts
    if diff < 60:
        return "now"
    minutes = diff // 60
    if minutes < 60:
        return f"{minutes} minute{'s' if minutes != 1 else ''} ago"
    hours = minutes // 60
    if hours < 24:
        return f"{hours} hour{'s' if hours != 1 else ''} ago"
    days = hours // 24
    if days < 7:
        return f"{days} day{'s' if days != 1 else ''} ago"
    weeks = days // 7
    if weeks < 5:
        return f"{weeks} week{'s' if weeks != 1 else ''} ago"
    months = days // 30
    if months < 12:
        return f"{months} month{'s' if months != 1 else ''} ago"
    years = days // 365
    return f"{years} year{'s' if years != 1 else ''} ago"


def list_files(cwd):
    rc, out, _ = run_git(cwd, "ls-files")
    if rc != 0:
        return []
    return [f for f in out.splitlines() if f.strip()]


def authors_info(cwd, limit, show_email=False):
    rc, out, _ = run_git(cwd, "log", "--pretty=format:%an|%ae")
    if rc != 0:
        return [], 0
    counts = {}
    emails = {}
    total = 0
    for line in out.splitlines():
        if "|" in line:
            name, email = line.split("|", 1)
        else:
            name, email = line, ""
        counts[name] = counts.get(name, 0) + 1
        emails.setdefault(name, email)
        total += 1
    sorted_a = sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda x: (-x[1], x[0]))
    result = []
    for name, n in sorted_a[:limit]:
        contribution = int(round(100.0 * n / total)) if total else 0
        result.append({
            "name": name,
            "email": emails[name] if show_email else None,
            "nbrOfCommits": n,
            "contribution": contribution,
        })
    return result, len(counts)


def total_commits(cwd):
    rc, out, _ = run_git(cwd, "rev-list", "--count", "HEAD")
    if rc == 0:
        return int(out.strip())
    return 0


def is_shallow(cwd):
    rc, out, _ = run_git(cwd, "rev-parse", "--is-shallow-repository")
    return out.strip() == "true"


def churn_info(cwd, limit, pool_size=None):
    # How many commits to consider?
    pool = pool_size if pool_size is not None else total_commits(cwd)
    rc, out, _ = run_git(cwd, "log", f"-n{pool}", "--name-only", "--pretty=format:")
    if rc != 0:
        return [], pool
    counts = {}
    for line in out.splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if line:
            counts[line] = counts.get(line, 0) + 1
    sorted_c = sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda x: (-x[1], x[0]))
    out_list = [{"filePath": f, "nbrOfCommits": c} for f, c in sorted_c[:limit]]
    return out_list, pool


def repo_size_and_file_count(cwd):
    rc, out, _ = run_git(cwd, "ls-tree", "-r", "-l", "HEAD")
    if rc != 0:
        return "0 B", 0
    total = 0
    count = 0
    for line in out.splitlines():
        parts = line.split()
        if len(parts) >= 4:
            try:
                total += int(parts[3])
                count += 1
            except ValueError:
                pass
    return human_size(total), count


def human_size(n):
    units = ["B", "KiB", "MiB", "GiB", "TiB"]
    i = 0
    f = float(n)
    while f >= 1024 and i < len(units) - 1:
        f /= 1024
        i += 1
    if i == 0:
        return f"{int(f)} {units[i]}"
    # 1 decimal to 2 sig figs
    if f >= 100:
        return f"{f:.0f} {units[i]}"
    return f"{f:.2f} {units[i]}"


def detect_license(cwd):
    for name in os.listdir(cwd):
        if name.upper().startswith("LICENSE") or name.upper().startswith("LICENCE") or name.upper().startswith("COPYING"):
            try:
                with open(os.path.join(cwd, name), "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
                    content = f.read()
                # Very simple detection
                if "MIT License" in content or "MIT LICENSE" in content.upper():
                    return "MIT"
                if "Apache License" in content:
                    return "Apache-2.0"
                if "GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE" in content.upper():
                    return "GPL"
                if "BSD" in content:
                    return "BSD"
                return ""
            except OSError:
                pass
    return ""


def repo_name(cwd):
    # Try remote URL
    rc, out, _ = run_git(cwd, "config", "--get", "remote.origin.url")
    if rc == 0 and out.strip():
        url = out.strip()
        name = url.rstrip("/").split("/")[-1]
        if name.endswith(".git"):
            name = name[:-4]
        return name, url
    return "", ""


def detect_languages(cwd, files, types_filter):
    """Very basic language detection based on file extensions."""
    # Count bytes per language
    ext_map = {
        ".py": ("Python", "programming"),
        ".rs": ("Rust", "programming"),
        ".c": ("C", "programming"),
        ".h": ("C Header", "programming"),
        ".cpp": ("C++", "programming"),
        ".cc": ("C++", "programming"),
        ".hpp": ("C++", "programming"),
        ".go": ("Go", "programming"),
        ".java": ("Java", "programming"),
        ".js": ("JavaScript", "programming"),
        ".ts": ("TypeScript", "programming"),
        ".jsx": ("JSX", "programming"),
        ".tsx": ("TSX", "programming"),
        ".sh": ("Shell", "programming"),
        ".rb": ("Ruby", "programming"),
        ".php": ("PHP", "programming"),
        ".md": ("Markdown", "prose"),
        ".html": ("HTML", "markup"),
        ".css": ("CSS", "markup"),
        ".xml": ("XML", "data"),
        ".json": ("JSON", "data"),
        ".yml": ("YAML", "data"),
        ".yaml": ("YAML", "data"),
        ".toml": ("TOML", "data"),
        ".txt": ("Plain Text", "prose"),
    }
    counts = {}
    total = 0
    for f in files:
        full = os.path.join(cwd, f)
        try:
            size = os.path.getsize(full)
        except OSError:
            continue
        _, ext = os.path.splitext(f)
        ext = ext.lower()
        if ext in ext_map:
            lang, ty = ext_map[ext]
            if ty in types_filter:
                counts[lang] = counts.get(lang, 0) + size
                total += size
    if total == 0:
        return []
    items = sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])
    return [{"language": k, "percentage": round(v * 100.0 / total, 1)} for k, v in items]


def lines_of_code(cwd, files, types_filter):
    """Count total lines of code across known source files."""
    total = 0
    ext_map = {".py",".rs",".c",".h",".cpp",".cc",".hpp",".go",".java",".js",".ts",".jsx",".tsx",".sh",".rb",".php"}
    for f in files:
        _, ext = os.path.splitext(f)
        if ext.lower() not in ext_map:
            continue
        full = os.path.join(cwd, f)
        try:
            with open(full, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fp:
                for line in fp:
                    total += 1
        except OSError:
            pass
    return total


# --- Output builders ---

def format_number(n, sep):
    s = str(n)
    if sep == "plain":
        return s
    m = {"comma": ",", "space": " ", "underscore": "_"}.get(sep, "")
    # Group by 3 from right
    parts = []
    i = len(s)
    while i > 3:
        parts.insert(0, s[i-3:i])
        i -= 3
    parts.insert(0, s[:i])
    return m.join(parts)


def build_info_struct(args, cwd):
    repoName, repoUrl = repo_name(cwd)
    sha, refs = head_refs(cwd)
    added, deleted, modified = pending_info(cwd)
    created, last_change = created_and_last_change(cwd, iso=args.iso_time)
    authors_list, total_authors = authors_info(cwd, args.number_of_authors, show_email=args.email)
    commits_n = total_commits(cwd)
    shallow = is_shallow(cwd)
    files = list_files(cwd)
    types_filter = set(args.type)
    langs = detect_languages(cwd, files, types_filter)
    loc = lines_of_code(cwd, files, types_filter)
    churns, pool = churn_info(cwd, args.number_of_file_churns, pool_size=args.churn_pool_size)
    size, file_count = repo_size_and_file_count(cwd)
    license_name = detect_license(cwd)

    info_fields = []

    def disabled(name):
        return name in args.disabled_fields

    if not disabled("project"):
        info_fields.append({"ProjectInfo": {"repoName": repoName, "numberOfBranches": 0, "numberOfTags": 0}})
    if not disabled("description"):
        info_fields.append({"DescriptionInfo": {"description": None}})
    if not disabled("head"):
        info_fields.append({"HeadInfo": {"headRefs": {"shortCommitId": sha, "refs": refs}}})
    if not disabled("pending") and (added or deleted or modified):
        info_fields.append({"PendingInfo": {"added": added, "deleted": deleted, "modified": modified}})
    if not disabled("version"):
        info_fields.append({"VersionInfo": {"version": ""}})
    if not disabled("created"):
        info_fields.append({"CreatedInfo": {"creationDate": created}})
    if not disabled("languages") and langs:
        info_fields.append({"LanguagesInfo": {"languagesWithPercentage": langs}})
    if not disabled("dependencies"):
        info_fields.append({"DependenciesInfo": {"dependencies": ""}})
    if not disabled("authors"):
        info_fields.append({"AuthorsInfo": {"authors": authors_list}})
    if not disabled("last-change"):
        info_fields.append({"LastChangeInfo": {"lastChange": last_change}})
    if not disabled("contributors"):
        info_fields.append({"ContributorsInfo": {"totalNumberOfAuthors": total_authors}})
    if not disabled("url"):
        info_fields.append({"UrlInfo": {"repoUrl": repoUrl}})
    if not disabled("commits"):
        info_fields.append({"CommitsInfo": {"numberOfCommits": commits_n, "isShallow": shallow}})
    if not disabled("churn"):
        info_fields.append({"ChurnInfo": {"file_churns": churns, "churn_pool_size": pool}})
    if not disabled("lines-of-code") and loc > 0:
        info_fields.append({"LocInfo": {"linesOfCode": loc}})
    if not disabled("size"):
        info_fields.append({"SizeInfo": {"repoSize": size, "fileCount": file_count}})
    if not disabled("license"):
        info_fields.append({"LicenseInfo": {"license": license_name}})

    title = {
        "gitUsername": get_git_username(cwd),
        "gitVersion": git_version(),
    }
    return {"title": title, "infoFields": info_fields}


def get_git_username(cwd):
    # onefetch uses project directory name in some contexts, here we use user.name
    rc, out, _ = run_git(cwd, "config", "--get", "user.name")
    if rc == 0 and out.strip():
        return out.strip()
    return ""


def to_yaml(data, indent=0):
    """Very simple YAML serializer matching observed format."""
    out = []
    prefix = "  " * indent
    if isinstance(data, dict):
        for k, v in data.items():
            if isinstance(v, (dict, list)):
                if isinstance(v, list) and not v:
                    out.append(f"{prefix}{k}: []")
                elif isinstance(v, dict) and not v:
                    out.append(f"{prefix}{k}: {{}}")
                else:
                    out.append(f"{prefix}{k}:")
                    out.append(to_yaml(v, indent + 1))
            else:
                out.append(f"{prefix}{k}: {yaml_scalar(v)}")
    elif isinstance(data, list):
        for item in data:
            if isinstance(item, dict):
                # First key goes with dash
                keys = list(item.keys())
                first_k = keys[0]
                first_v = item[first_k]
                if isinstance(first_v, (dict, list)):
                    out.append(f"{prefix}- {first_k}:")
                    out.append(to_yaml(first_v, indent + 2))
                else:
                    out.append(f"{prefix}- {first_k}: {yaml_scalar(first_v)}")
                for k in keys[1:]:
                    v = item[k]
                    if isinstance(v, (dict, list)):
                        out.append(f"{prefix}  {k}:")
                        out.append(to_yaml(v, indent + 2))
                    else:
                        out.append(f"{prefix}  {k}: {yaml_scalar(v)}")
            else:
                out.append(f"{prefix}- {yaml_scalar(item)}")
    return "\n".join(out)


def yaml_scalar(v):
    if v is None:
        return "null"
    if isinstance(v, bool):
        return "true" if v else "false"
    if isinstance(v, (int, float)):
        return str(v)
    if isinstance(v, str):
        if v == "":
            return "''"
        return v
    return str(v)


def output_json(data):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(data, indent=2))
    sys.stdout.flush()


def output_yaml(data):
    sys.stdout.write(to_yaml(data))
    sys.stdout.write("\n")


# --- Main ---

def main(argv):
    load_resources_inline()
    args = parse_args(argv)

    if args.languages_flag:
        sys.stdout.write(RESOURCES["languages.txt"])
        return 0
    if args.package_managers_flag:
        sys.stdout.write(RESOURCES["package_managers.txt"])
        return 0
    if args.generate:
        keymap = {
            "bash": "complete_bash.sh",
            "zsh": "complete_zsh.zsh",
            "fish": "complete_fish.fish",
            "powershell": "complete_pwsh.ps1",
            "elvish": "complete_elvish.elv",
        }
        sys.stdout.write(RESOURCES[keymap[args.generate]])
        return 0

    # Determine working directory
    path = args.input or os.getcwd()
    if not os.path.isdir(path):
        sys.stderr.write(f"Error: Failed to access a directory, or path is not a directory: '{path}'\n")
        return 1
    abspath = os.path.abspath(path)

    # Image file special handling
    if args.image is not None:
        if not os.path.exists(args.image):
            sys.stderr.write(f"Error: Could not load the image file at '{args.image}'\n\n")
            sys.stderr.write("Caused by:\n")
            sys.stderr.write("    No such file or directory (os error 2)\n")
            return 1

    repo = find_repo(abspath)
    if repo is None:
        sys.stderr.write(f"Error: Could not find a git repository in '{abspath}' or in any of its parents\n")
        return 1
    cwd = repo[0]

    data = build_info_struct(args, cwd)
    if args.output == "json":
        output_json(data)
    elif args.output == "yaml":
        output_yaml(data)
    else:
        render_terminal(args, data, cwd)
    return 0


def render_terminal(args, data, cwd):
    """Terminal render: print title header and info lines with ANSI colors."""
    # Very basic rendering; not attempting to match ASCII art
    # Based on observed output: header includes user, separator, fields with colon
    # Using [37;1m style bold ANSI for labels.
    BOLD = "\033[1m"
    RESET = "\033[0m"
    # Colors indices: title=37;1 ~=39;1 underline=37;1 subtitle=39;1 colon=39;1 info=39
    # Allow override via args.text_colors
    def esc(code):
        return f"\033[{code}m"
    tcols = args.text_colors if args.text_colors else []
    def c(idx, default):
        if idx < len(tcols):
            n = int(tcols[idx])
            # ANSI 30+ for base; clap converts 0..15 to escapes
            # 0-7 -> 30-37, 8-15 -> 90-97
            if n < 8:
                return f"{30 + n};1"
            else:
                return f"{90 + (n - 8)};1"
        return default
    title_c = c(0, "37;1")
    tilde_c = c(1, "39;1")
    underline_c = c(2, "37;1")
    subtitle_c = c(3, "39;1")
    colon_c = c(4, "39;1")
    info_c = c(5, "39")
    if args.no_bold:
        # Remove ";1" from codes
        def strip1(x):
            return x.replace(";1", "")
        title_c = strip1(title_c)
        tilde_c = strip1(tilde_c)
        underline_c = strip1(underline_c)
        subtitle_c = strip1(subtitle_c)
        colon_c = strip1(colon_c)
        info_c = strip1(info_c)

    sys.stdout.write("\033[?7l")
    title = data["title"]
    user = title["gitUsername"]
    gv = title["gitVersion"]
    header = f"{esc(title_c)}{user}\033[0m {esc(tilde_c)}~\033[0m {esc(title_c)}{gv}\033[0m"
    sys.stdout.write(header + "\n")
    # underline length = len(user + " ~ " + gv) without ANSI
    plain_len = len(user) + 3 + len(gv)
    sys.stdout.write(f"{esc(underline_c.replace(';1',''))}" + "-" * plain_len + "\033[39m\n")
    # each info field
    for field in data["infoFields"]:
        key, val = next(iter(field.items()))
        rendered = render_field(key, val, args)
        for line in rendered:
            sys.stdout.write(
                f"{esc(subtitle_c)}{line['label']}\033[0m{esc(colon_c)}{line.get('colon',':')}\033[0m {esc(info_c)}{line['value']}\033[0m\n"
                if line.get('label') else
                f"{esc(info_c)}{line['value']}\033[0m\n"
            )
    # Color palette
    sys.stdout.write("\n")
    palette = ""
    for i in range(8):
        palette += f"\033[4{i}m   \033[49m"
    sys.stdout.write(palette + "\n")
    sys.stdout.write("\033[?7h")


def render_field(key, val, args):
    out = []
    if key == "HeadInfo":
        hr = val["headRefs"]
        refs = ", ".join(hr["refs"]) if hr["refs"] else ""
        v = hr["shortCommitId"]
        if refs:
            v += f" ({refs})"
        out.append({"label": "HEAD", "value": v})
    elif key == "PendingInfo":
        parts = []
        if val["added"]:
            parts.append(f"{val['added']}+")
        if val["deleted"]:
            parts.append(f"{val['deleted']}-")
        if val["modified"]:
            parts.append(f"{val['modified']}M")
        out.append({"label": "Pending", "value": " ".join(parts)})
    elif key == "CreatedInfo":
        out.append({"label": "Created", "value": val["creationDate"]})
    elif key == "AuthorsInfo":
        authors = val["authors"]
        if authors:
            for i, a in enumerate(authors):
                label = "Author" if i == 0 else ""
                v = f"{a['contribution']}% {a['name']} {a['nbrOfCommits']}"
                if a.get("email"):
                    v = f"{a['contribution']}% {a['name']} <{a['email']}> {a['nbrOfCommits']}"
                out.append({"label": label, "value": v, "colon": ":" if i == 0 else " "})
    elif key == "LastChangeInfo":
        out.append({"label": "Last change", "value": val["lastChange"]})
    elif key == "CommitsInfo":
        v = str(val["numberOfCommits"])
        if val["isShallow"]:
            v += " (shallow)"
        out.append({"label": "Commits", "value": v})
    elif key == "ChurnInfo":
        churns = val["file_churns"]
        if churns:

def similar_name(value, candidates):
    """Simple similarity: pick candidate with smallest edit distance."""
    if not candidates:
        return None
    best = None
    best_d = None
    for c in candidates:
        d = edit_distance(value, c)
        if best_d is None or d < best_d:
            best_d = d
            best = c
    if best_d is not None and best_d <= max(2, len(value) // 2):
        return best
    return None


def edit_distance(a, b):
    la, lb = len(a), len(b)
    dp = list(range(lb + 1))
    for i in range(1, la + 1):
        prev = dp[0]
        dp[0] = i
        for j in range(1, lb + 1):
            tmp = dp[j]
            if a[i-1] == b[j-1]:
                dp[j] = prev
            else:
                dp[j] = 1 + min(prev, dp[j], dp[j-1])
            prev = tmp
    return dp[lb]

def load_resources_inline():

        return

    raw = zlib.decompress(base64.b64decode(idx))
    # Format: for each entry: name\n<len>\n<data>
    pos = 0
    data = raw
    while pos < len(data):

        name = data[pos:nl].decode()
        pos = nl + 1
        nl2 = data.index(b"\n", pos)
        length = int(data[pos:nl2])
        pos = nl2 + 1
        content = data[pos:pos+length].decode()
        pos += length
        RESOURCES[name] = content

def run_git(cwd, *args):
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["git"] + list(args), cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False
        )
        return result.returncode, result.stdout, result.stderr
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return 127, "", "git not found"


def find_repo(path):
    """Walk up to find a .git dir or file. Return (repo_root, git_dir) or None."""
    p = os.path.abspath(path)
    while True:
        g = os.path.join(p, ".git")
        if os.path.exists(g):
            return p, g
        parent = os.path.dirname(p)
        if parent == p:
            return None
        p = parent


def git_version():

        refs.append(out.strip())
    # Add tags
    rc, out, _ = run_git(cwd, "tag", "--points-at", "HEAD")
    if rc == 0:
        for line in out.strip().splitlines():
            if line.strip():
                refs.append(line.strip())
    return sha, refs

    added = deleted = modified = 0
    if rc == 0:
        for line in out.splitlines():
            if len(line) < 2:
                continue
            xy = line[:2]
            if "?" in xy or "A" in xy:
                added += 1
            elif "D" in xy:
                deleted += 1
            elif "M" in xy or "R" in xy or "C" in xy or "U" in xy or "T" in xy:
                modified += 1
    return added, deleted, modified


def created_and_last_change(cwd, iso=False):
    # first commit and last commit
    rc, first, _ = run_git(cwd, "log", "--reverse", "--pretty=format:%at", "--max-parents=0")
    rc2, last, _ = run_git(cwd, "log", "-1", "--pretty=format:%at")
    def fmt(ts):
        if iso:
            return datetime.fromtimestamp(int(ts), tz=timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
        return humanize_ago(int(ts))
    created = ""
    last_change = ""
    if rc == 0 and first.strip():
        first_ts = first.strip().splitlines()[0]
        created = fmt(first_ts)
    if rc2 == 0 and last.strip():
        last_change = fmt(last.strip())
    return created, last_change


def humanize_ago(ts):
    now = int(datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc).timestamp())
    diff = now - ts
    if diff < 60:
        return "now"
    minutes = diff // 60
    if minutes < 60:
        return f"{minutes} minute{'s' if minutes != 1 else ''} ago"
    hours = minutes // 60
    if hours < 24:
        return f"{hours} hour{'s' if hours != 1 else ''} ago"
    days = hours // 24
    if days < 7:
        return f"{days} day{'s' if days != 1 else ''} ago"
    weeks = days // 7
    if weeks < 5:
        return f"{weeks} week{'s' if weeks != 1 else ''} ago"
    months = days // 30
    if months < 12:
        return f"{months} month{'s' if months != 1 else ''} ago"
    years = days // 365
    return f"{years} year{'s' if years != 1 else ''} ago"

def authors_info(cwd, limit, show_email=False):
    rc, out, _ = run_git(cwd, "log", "--pretty=format:%an|%ae")
    if rc != 0:
        return [], 0
    counts = {}
    emails = {}
    total = 0
    for line in out.splitlines():
        if "|" in line:
            name, email = line.split("|", 1)
        else:
            name, email = line, ""
        counts[name] = counts.get(name, 0) + 1
        emails.setdefault(name, email)
        total += 1
    sorted_a = sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda x: (-x[1], x[0]))
    result = []
    for name, n in sorted_a[:limit]:
        contribution = int(round(100.0 * n / total)) if total else 0
        result.append({
            "name": name,
            "email": emails[name] if show_email else None,
            "nbrOfCommits": n,
            "contribution": contribution,
        })
    return result, len(counts)

def churn_info(cwd, limit, pool_size=None):

    pool = pool_size if pool_size is not None else total_commits(cwd)
    rc, out, _ = run_git(cwd, "log", f"-n{pool}", "--name-only", "--pretty=format:")
    if rc != 0:
        return [], pool
    counts = {}
    for line in out.splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if line:
            counts[line] = counts.get(line, 0) + 1
    sorted_c = sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda x: (-x[1], x[0]))
    out_list = [{"filePath": f, "nbrOfCommits": c} for f, c in sorted_c[:limit]]
    return out_list, pool


def repo_size_and_file_count(cwd):

    if rc != 0:
        return "0 B", 0
    total = 0
    count = 0
    for line in out.splitlines():
        parts = line.split()
        if len(parts) >= 4:
            try:
                total += int(parts[3])
                count += 1
            except ValueError:

def human_size(n):
    units = ["B", "KiB", "MiB", "GiB", "TiB"]
    i = 0
    f = float(n)
    while f >= 1024 and i < len(units) - 1:
        f /= 1024
        i += 1
    if i == 0:
        return f"{int(f)} {units[i]}"
    # 1 decimal to 2 sig figs
    if f >= 100:
        return f"{f:.0f} {units[i]}"
    return f"{f:.2f} {units[i]}"


def detect_license(cwd):
    for name in os.listdir(cwd):
        if name.upper().startswith("LICENSE") or name.upper().startswith("LICENCE") or name.upper().startswith("COPYING"):
            try:
                with open(os.path.join(cwd, name), "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
                    content = f.read()
                # Very simple detection
                if "MIT License" in content or "MIT LICENSE" in content.upper():
                    return "MIT"
                if "Apache License" in content:
                    return "Apache-2.0"
                if "GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE" in content.upper():
                    return "GPL"
                if "BSD" in content:
                    return "BSD"
                return ""
            except OSError:
                pass
    return ""
